notes: NO QUESTABLE CONTENT. Empty chain is deliberate and the reason is unusual enough to be worth the whole note. WHAT society ACTUALLY IS. The modid society belongs to a Modrinth mod whose SLUG is society-tweaks and whose displayName is plain 'Society' - META-INF/mods.toml reads modId="society", version="1.22", displayName="Society", loaderVersion="[47,)". It is 1.20.1 Forge, 77.8K downloads. Searching Modrinth for 'society' as a slug returns 404; the top search hit is society-sunlit-valley, which is a MODPACK (project_type: modpack), not a mod. That is three separate name traps stacked on one namespace: the modid is society, the mod slug is society-tweaks, and the most prominent thing called Society is a modpack that merely contains it. THE JAR REGISTERS SIX ITEMS. It is a 70MB jar and almost all of that is assets - assets/society has 1574 files, plus bundled assets/dialog (60) and assets/kata (45) namespaces - because Society Tweaks is an NPC, dialogue and cutscene framework, not a content mod. Two independent passes agree: models/item stems INTERSECT lang keys gives 6, and an independent rebuild from recipe results, loot tables, blockstates and lang keys gives 7, the single difference being berry_bush, a model-only stem with zero data references. data/society contains just 12 files and NOT ONE RECIPE and NOT ONE LOOT TABLE. The six ids are society:face_note, society:invitation, society:monocle, society:red_glasses, society:spiral_glasses and society:villager, and every one of them has ZERO references anywhere in data/ - no recipe, no loot, no trade, no advancement. They are handed out by the framework's dialogue scripts. So there is nothing in this jar a survival quest can ask for. THE 26 CONSENSUS IDS ARE NOT IN THE MOD AT ALL, and this is the finding that matters. moddb.json lists 26 society: ids from 6 packs - jasper, mossberry, topaz, toy_train, tigerseye, green_tea_honeycomb, hematite, petrified_slime, galaxy_sword, animal_feed, princess_hairbrush, jamborite, fish_pond_basket, slate, source_gem, orpiment, amethyst_chunk, caterpillar_eggs, artisan_hopper, holy_symbol, celestine, ribbit_hut, auto_grabber, lemon_stone, invitation and mini_oni_eye. Matched against the jar's id set, ZERO of the 26 resolve (invitation is the one near-miss - it IS a real jar id, and it is the only one). I chased where the other 25 come from by downloading Society-Sunlit-Valley-4.1.4.mrpack (74MB) and reading it: the pack's overrides/kubejs/startup_scripts directory registers them. registerItems.js, registerBlocks.js, registerWeapons.js and globalRegistry.js create items into the society namespace, and a text scan of the pack finds 929 distinct society: ids across its overrides - jasper appears in crystalarium.js, fishPondDefinitions.js and globalRegistry.js; galaxy_sword in registerWeapons.js; topaz in crystalarium.js, recyclingMachine.js and modifyItems.js; animal_feed in feedingTrough.js and prizeMachine.js; mossberry in dehydrator.js, preservesJar.js and wineKeg.js; toy_train in globalRegistry.js. There is also overrides/kubejs/assets/society/ carrying its own lang, models and blockstates for them. CONCLUSION AND WHAT TO DO. society: items are PACK CONTENT, not mod content. They exist only when the Society: Sunlit Valley modpack (or a sibling built on the same KubeJS - Society: Sunlit Cobblemon, Society Trading, Sunlit Cobblemon Tweaks) is installed, and they cannot be obtained by adding a mod to another pack. Installing society-tweaks alone gives you six dialogue props and nothing else. A generator must therefore SKIP this namespace for any pack that is not itself a Society pack, which is what the empty chain plus this marker achieves. If the target pack IS a Society pack, the ids are real but they must be read out of that pack's own overrides/kubejs/startup_scripts, not out of any jar - and a fresh research pass against the pack, not the mod, would be needed to write a chain. NOTHING WAS INVENTED HERE: no chain step and no wheel is emitted, because every id that would make a good quest lives outside the artifact this file is allowed to verify against.
